section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the soul's descent into the body is not for its own sake, but to refine the body, animal soul, and one's portion in the world, thereby making a dwelling place for G-d in the lowest realm, which is the work of "taking the stones of the place."
section.t: And this is that the service after "Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva and went to Charan"
(the descent of the soul into the body)
is "and he took from the stones of the place, etc."
For it is known
that the intention of the soul's descent below is not for the sake of the soul, but rather in order to refine and purify the body, the animal soul, and its portion in the world,
for specifically through this is revealed the intention that
the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to have for Himself a dwelling place in the lower realms,
in the lowest realm, beneath which there is no lower.
And this is that the primary service of the soul in its descent below
("Yaakov went out etc. to Charan")
is "and he took from the stones of the place, etc.,"
"place" being an existence in which the G-dly light within it is in concealment and hiding
[and as above
(section 6)
that this that the Name Havayah
(in its squared spelling)
has the numerical value of "place" — the intention in this is,
that the Name Havayah is in concealment and hiding within the place
(in a manner of numerical value).
For although the entire existence of place
(the world)
is that the Name Havayah constantly brings it into being from nothing to something,
nevertheless, the manner of the existence of the Name Havayah in the world is only in a manner of numerical value,
a level of concealment and hiding],
and within this itself — "the stones of the place,"
"stones" in the plural
(as above),
and the ultimate purpose of the soul's descent below
("Yaakov went out etc. to Charan")
is
(not for the sake of the light drawn to it through Torah and mitzvos,
but rather)
for the sake of the service of "and he took from the stones of the place,"
to take the lower things
(the body, animal soul, and its portion in the world),
and in a manner of "and he took," that he becomes master, ruler, and governor over them,
and to make of them a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section adds that refining permissible things for the sake of Heaven has an advantage over refining physical things through mitzvos, as it more fully completes the intention of a dwelling place in the lowest realm.
section.t: And one may add,

that in the matter of refinements themselves, there is an advantage to the refinement of permissible things by doing them for the sake of Heaven over the refinement of physical things through the performance of mitzvos,
for through the refinement of permissible things
(that even when one does them for the sake of Heaven, they remain permissible things,
"your deeds")
the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms is more fully completed,
the lowest realm beneath which there is no lower.
And based on this, it will be better understood that the service
(for which the soul descended below)
is "and he took from the stones of the place,"
for "place" is an existence in which the G-dly light within it is in concealment and hiding, as above,
and it can be said
that it refers
(primarily)
to permissible things,
for even after the service they are "your deeds" of the person.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the great ascent of the stones of the place, after refinement, reaches above Yaakov's head, culminating in "this stone shall be a house of G-d," referring to a dwelling for G-d's very Essence, which is the ultimate purpose of creation.
section.t: And 4)
And based on this, one can also understand the greatness of the ascent of the stones of the place
[after they become one stone,
through the service of refinements],
that they ascend above the level of the head of Yaakov
("and he placed them at his headrest"),
and until
(after the completion of the refinements)
"and this stone etc. shall be a house of G-d,"
that the intention in this is
(as above, section 1)
not to "G-d" in a general sense, but to the level of "and Havayah shall be my G-d."
For it is known
that the ultimate true intention in the creation and coming into being of the worlds is that which the Holy One, blessed be He, desired, to have for Himself a dwelling place in the lower realms,
in this physical world, beneath which there is no lower.
For although there are several reasons for the creation of the world
[so that they should know Him
and in order that the perfection of His powers be revealed, etc.],
these reasons are in the souls of Atzilus
(the reason of "so that they should know")
and in the level of Atzilus
(the reason of "in order that they be revealed"),
and the place and root of these reasons is in the level of revelations.
However, the matter of the Holy One, blessed be He, desiring to have for Himself a dwelling place in the lower realms
[that from this aspect it was necessary for the coming into being of this lower world specifically, beneath which there is no lower]
is in His very Essence.
And as the Alter Rebbe said
(regarding the matter of the desire for a dwelling place in the lower realms)
"Upon a desire, there is no question,"
for the matter of desire is in His very Essence, where the matter of questions does not apply.
And this is "and this stone etc. shall be a house of G-d,"
that the intention of "G-d" here is for the level of the essential concealment,
that specifically physical things
(the level of stone,
inanimate)
shall be a house and dwelling place for His very Essence, blessed be He.
